mainTopic: Using a vessel for an egg laid on שבת: רבה's common-case rule, רב יוסף's מבטל כלי מהיכנו, and רבי יצחק's rule that a vessel may only be moved for something movable.
overview: On the previous amud, רב חסדא ruled that on שבת you may cover an egg to protect it, but you may not place a vessel under a hen to catch its egg. רבה explained that חכמים allowed moving a vessel to prevent a loss only in common situations. אביי challenged him three times (a lamp, a broken beam, a leak), and each time רבה showed that the case really was common. רב יוסף then gave a different reason: catching the egg traps the vessel holding something מוקצה, which is מבטל כלי מהיכנו. אביי challenged this with several cases: טבל, sparks, a beam, a leak, and a basket for chicks. Each is answered by showing the vessel never really becomes unusable. The basket discussion also teaches that anything מוקצה during בין השמשות stays מוקצה all day. רבי יצחק is stricter: you may not even cover the egg, because a vessel may only be moved for something that may itself be moved. The challenges to him are answered with צריך למקומו, or by showing the item is not מוקצה (stones, bricks, a hive with honey). רב עוקבא ממישן's question on the honey answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from covering a lamp
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with a ברייתא: one may turn a bowl over a lamp so the fire won't catch the beam, which seems to be an uncommon danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: we learned that one may turn a bowl upside down over a lamp so that the fire will not catch onto the roof beam!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's rule that חכמים only permitted moving a vessel for a common situation. Here a vessel is used to prevent a fire, which seems rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said moving a vessel to prevent loss is allowed only when the danger is common. A lamp setting a beam on fire seems unusual, yet the ברייתא permits covering it. So it looks like even uncommon dangers allow using a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from an earlier source)

phrases.english: He challenged him: one may turn a bowl over the lamp
phrases.notes: אביי is objecting to רבה.

phrases.english: so that the fire will not catch the beam?
phrases.notes: The point: preventing what seems like a rare fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the attack on רבה's explanation of רב חסדא (stated on the previous amud).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that חכמים permitted moving a vessel only for a common situation (דבר המצוי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lamp catching the beam seems uncommon, yet using a bowl is permitted, which contradicts the 'common cases only' rule.

steps.title: Low houses often catch fire
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא is about low-ceilinged houses, where fires are common.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about low houses, where fires are common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his rule. He says the lamp case is actually a common danger, because it is about houses with low ceilings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a low house the flame sits close to the beam, so fires happen often. That makes the case a דבר המצוי, and it fits רבה's rule perfectly.

phrases.english: It is talking about low houses
phrases.notes: Low ceilings put the beam close to the flame.

phrases.english: where fire is common.
phrases.notes: So this is a common case after all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the source deals with a situation where the danger is common.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamp case was about an unusual danger.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamp case is about low houses where fire is common, so it fits the 'common cases only' rule.

steps.title: Challenge from propping up a broken beam
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: a broken beam may be propped up with a bench or bed-frame pieces, even though beams breaking seems uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, a beam that broke may be supported with a bench or with the long sides of a bed!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second source against רבה. Here too, vessels are moved to prevent a loss that seems rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken roof beam does not seem like an everyday event. Yet the source permits moving a bench or bed parts to hold it up. This again suggests that uncommon situations also allow using vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: The long side-boards of a bed frame

phrases.english: And similarly, a beam that broke,
phrases.notes: וכן signals another source with the same difficulty.

phrases.english: one may support it with a bench and with the long sides of a bed!
phrases.notes: Moving vessels to prevent a seemingly rare collapse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same kind as step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A beam breaking seems unusual, yet moving vessels to support it is permitted.

steps.title: New beams often crack
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the case is about new beams, which commonly crack.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about new beams, which tend to crack.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה again shows that the case is really a common one. New beams often split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh, new wood often cracks as it dries. So a breaking beam in this case is a דבר המצוי, and the source does not disprove רבה.

phrases.english: It is talking about new beams
phrases.notes: New wood behaves differently from old wood.

phrases.english: which tend to crack.
phrases.notes: So the danger is common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a common situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A beam breaking is a rare event.
steps.terutzMaskana: With new beams, cracking is common, so the rule still holds.

steps.title: Challenge from placing a vessel under a leak
steps.stepSummary: A third challenge: one may place a vessel under a leak in the roof on שבת, even though leaks seem uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned that one may place a vessel under a leak on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a third source. A vessel is placed under a leak to catch the water, which again seems like an uncommon situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roof leaking seems like an unusual event, not a דבר המצוי. Yet the source permits placing a vessel under it on שבת. So again it looks like even uncommon losses allow using a vessel, against רבה's rule.

phrases.english: One may place a vessel under a leak on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: Very similar to placing a vessel under a hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge in the same series.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A leak seems unusual, yet placing a vessel under it is permitted.

steps.title: New houses often leak
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the case is about new houses, which frequently leak.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about new houses, which often leak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the same kind of answer a third time. New houses often leak, so the case is common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new roof has not settled yet, so leaks are frequent. That makes this a דבר המצוי, and רבה's rule survives all three challenges.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule: חכמים permitted moving a vessel to prevent loss only in common situations. Every challenge is answered by showing that the case really was common: low houses, new beams, new houses.

phrases.english: It is talking about new houses
phrases.notes: New roofs have not settled yet.

phrases.english: which commonly leak.
phrases.notes: So this too is a common case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and closes the series of challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a common situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A leaking roof is an uncommon event.
steps.terutzMaskana: New houses leak often, so the rule still holds.

steps.title: A different reason: the vessel becomes unusable
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives another reason for רב חסדא: catching the egg in a vessel takes the vessel out of use, which is called מבטל כלי מהיכנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: this is the reason of רב חסדא: because he takes a vessel out of its ready-for-use state.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a completely different explanation for why you may not put a vessel under a hen. His reason has nothing to do with common or uncommon cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg laid on שבת is מוקצה and may not be moved. Once it falls into the vessel, the vessel cannot be moved either, so it has been made useless for שבת. Making a vessel useless like this, as if fixing it in place, is forbidden. That is מבטל כלי מהיכנו.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a vessel out of its ready-for-use state
An item that may not be moved on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב יוסף is answering אביי's challenges. He is offering a separate reason for רב חסדא. His reason works whether the situation is common or not.
steps.whyThisMatters: מבטל כלי מהיכנו is an important שבת principle. It explains why you may not put a vessel in a spot where something מוקצה will fall into it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for רב חסדא. רבה says the permission covers only common situations. רב יוסף says it is because of מבטל כלי מהיכנו: the vessel becomes stuck holding a מוקצה egg.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said,
phrases.notes: A new voice with a new approach.

phrases.english: this is the reason of Rav Chisda:
phrases.notes: Explains why one may not put a vessel under a hen.

phrases.english: because he takes a vessel out of its ready-for-use state.
phrases.notes: The egg is מוקצה, so the vessel holding it can no longer be moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבה's line of reasoning and offers a different reason for רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not place a vessel under a hen to catch its egg, because the egg is מוקצה and catching it makes the vessel unmovable. This is forbidden as מבטל כלי מהיכנו.

steps.title: A broken barrel of untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף from a ruling that lets one put a vessel under a broken barrel of טבל on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: If a barrel of untithed produce broke, a person may bring another vessel and put it underneath! But טבל may not be used on שבת, so the vessel should become unusable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's idea that you may not make a vessel unusable on שבת. He brings a case where the law lets you put a vessel under a broken barrel of טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is produce that has not had its tithes taken. It may not be eaten, and it seems to be מוקצה on שבת. If the vessel catches טבל, it should become 'stuck' holding something forbidden, which is exactly what רב יוסף said is not allowed. Yet the ruling permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from a teaching of the חכמים)
Produce from which the מעשרות have not yet been taken; forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
A barrel of untithed produce that broke —
phrases.notes: This happened on שבת.

phrases.english: one brings another vessel and places it underneath it!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark shows that this is a challenge: the vessel seems to become unusable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's reason from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that one may not make a vessel unusable (מבטל כלי מהיכנו).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel catches טבל, which seems to be מוקצה. That should make the vessel unusable, yet the ruling allows it.

steps.title: Untithed produce counts as ready for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that טבל is considered prepared for שבת, because if someone did tithe it on שבת, it would become permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Untithed produce counts as ready for use on שבת. If a person went ahead and tithed it anyway, it is fixed and permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that טבל is not truly מוקצה. So a vessel holding it is not made unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing on שבת is forbidden. But if someone did it anyway, the produce would really become fixed and permitted. Since the produce can become usable on שבת itself, it counts as 'ready' (מוכן). The vessel is therefore holding something usable and is not ruined for use.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared or ready for use on שבת (the opposite of מוקצה)
He went ahead (did something forbidden) and tithed it
It is fixed, meaning properly tithed and permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT mean you may tithe on שבת. It only means that the produce is considered 'ready' for שבת, because the forbidden act would still work if someone did it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טֶבֶל מוּכָן הוּא אֵצֶל שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: He said to him: Untithed produce is prepared with regard to Shabbat,
for if one transgressed and tithed it — it is fixed.
phrases.notes: The act was forbidden, but it still works.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טֶבֶל מוּכָן הוּא אֵצֶל שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the contents: טבל is not truly מוקצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: טבל is forbidden, so it is מוקצה, and the vessel becomes unusable.
steps.terutzMaskana: טבל counts as ready (מוכן) for שבת, so the vessel still holds something usable.

steps.title: A vessel under a lamp to catch sparks
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges again from the rule that one may put a vessel under a lamp to catch sparks.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may put a vessel under a lamp to catch the sparks! The sparks are מוקצה, so the vessel should become unusable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second case against רב יוסף: a vessel placed under a lamp to catch falling sparks of burning oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sparks come from the lamp and are מוקצה. Once they land in the vessel, the vessel seems to become a base for something מוקצה and can no longer be moved. Yet the law permits putting it there.

keyTerms.meaning: Sparks (burning drops falling from the wick)

phrases.english: We may place a vessel under the lamp
to catch sparks!
phrases.notes: Another challenge to רב יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת הַנֵּר לְקַבֵּל נִיצוֹצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same rule, after step 9 answered the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule against making a vessel unusable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel catches מוקצה sparks, which should make it unusable, yet the ruling allows it.

steps.title: Sparks have no real substance
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that sparks have no substance, so nothing מוקצה actually stays in the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Sparks have no real substance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the sparks burn out and disappear. Nothing is left in the vessel to make it unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel only becomes unusable if something מוקצה actually sits in it. Sparks fade away as soon as they fall. So the vessel stays empty and can still be moved.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Sparks have no substance.
phrases.notes: They burn out, so nothing stays in the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: nothing מוקצה actually rests in the vessel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sparks fill the vessel with מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sparks disappear, so the vessel is never made unusable.

steps.title: Propping up a broken beam with a bench
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges from the rule that a broken beam may be supported with a bench or bed-frame pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise: a beam that broke may be supported with a bench or with the long side-boards of a bed! That should make the bench unusable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a third case: using a bench or bed boards to hold up a broken beam on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bench is holding up the beam, it seems you can no longer take it away. That would make the bench unusable on שבת. Yet this is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The long side-boards of a bed frame

steps.confusionAlert: This same case was used earlier (step 3) for a different question: whether the rule covers uncommon events. Here it is used against a different idea: making a vessel unusable.

phrases.english: And likewise, a beam that broke,

phrases.aramaic: סוֹמְכִין אוֹתָהּ בַּסַּפְסָל אוֹ בַּאֲרוּכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה!
phrases.english: we may support it with a bench or with the long boards of a bed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule against making a vessel unusable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holding up the beam ties up the bench, so it can no longer be used, yet this is allowed.

steps.title: The bench only supports the beam loosely
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the bench supports the beam only loosely, so it can still be taken away whenever one wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where it supports the beam loosely, so that if he wants, he can take the bench away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bench is not really stuck. It only touches the beam loosely and can be removed at any time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel is made 'unusable' only if it can no longer be taken. Here the bench is not carrying the full weight of the beam. So it stays available for use.

phrases.english: — where it is loose,
so that if he wants, he can take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the bench is only loosely in place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bench is locked in place holding the beam.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bench can still be removed, so it is not made unusable.

steps.title: A vessel under a dripping leak
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges from the rule that one may put a vessel under a leak on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may put a vessel under a leak on שבת! The dripping water seems to be מוקצה, so the vessel should become unusable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a fourth case: putting a vessel under water dripping from a leaky roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leak water seems useless and therefore מוקצה. Once it fills the vessel, the vessel could not be moved. Yet the law allows putting it there.

keyTerms.meaning: A leak; water dripping from the roof

phrases.english: We may place a vessel under a leak on Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth challenge to the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule against making a vessel unusable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel fills with water that seems מוקצה, yet this is allowed.

steps.title: The leak water is usable
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is about a leak whose water is fit to use, so it is not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a leak whose water is fit for use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the water is clean and usable. Because it is not מוקצה, the vessel is not ruined for use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessel only becomes unusable if what it holds is מוקצה. Usable water can be moved freely. So the vessel holding it can be moved too, and רב יוסף's rule stands after all four challenges.
steps.whatToRemember: These four challenges are answered the same basic way: the vessel never really becomes unusable. Either its contents are not מוקצה (טבל, usable water), nothing stays in it (sparks), or it can still be taken away (the loose bench). One more challenge to רב יוסף follows: the basket for chicks.

phrases.english: — With a leak that is fit for use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14; the next step brings one more challenge to רב יוסף (the basket for chicks).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the water is usable and not מוקצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leak water is useless and מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is about usable water, so the vessel stays usable.

steps.title: Challenge from turning a basket over for chicks
steps.stepSummary: Another challenge: a source allows turning a basket over so chicks can climb on and off it. This seems to make the basket unusable, since chicks are מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one may turn a basket upside down in front of chicks so that they can climb up and climb down!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more source to challenge the rule that you may not make a vessel unusable on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chicks are מוקצה. Once they stand on the basket, it seems the basket becomes a base for something מוקצה and can no longer be moved. If so, turning it over for them takes away the basket's usability, yet the source allows it.

phrases.english: One may turn a basket over in front of chicks
phrases.notes: Quoted from a תוספתא.

phrases.english: so that they can climb up and climb down!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks this as a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹפִין אֶת הַסַּל לִפְנֵי הָאֶפְרוֹחִין שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ וְיֵרְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge to רב יוסף's reason (step 7), following the four challenges in steps 8–15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule אין מבטלין כלי מהיכנו (one may not make a vessel unusable on שבת).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Letting מוקצה chicks stand on the basket seems to make the basket unmovable, yet the source allows it.

steps.title: The basket stays movable
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the basket may still be moved, so its usability is not taken away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that it is permitted to move it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. The basket does not become unmovable, so nothing was made unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the chicks make the basket מוקצה. This answer denies that: the basket can still be picked up, so the rule is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds / he is of the opinion

phrases.english: He holds it is permitted to move it.
phrases.notes: Sefaria identifies the one holding this as רב יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the challenge's assumption: the basket never becomes מוקצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chicks make the basket unmovable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket stays movable, so its usability is not lost.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the basket may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: a ברייתא explicitly says it is forbidden to move the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: it is forbidden to move it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer just given by quoting a source that forbids moving the basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the basket may be moved. This ברייתא says the opposite, so the answer seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: but was it not taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But it was taught: it is forbidden to move it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the basket may be moved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly forbids moving the basket.

steps.title: Forbidden only while the chicks are on it
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the ban applies only while the chicks are standing on the basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is while they are still on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the ברייתא: the basket is forbidden only while the chicks are on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the chicks climb off, the basket can be moved again. So its usability was never lost for good.

keyTerms.meaning: while they are still on it

phrases.english: While they are still on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids moving the basket at all times.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden only while the chicks are on it.

steps.title: Forbidden even after the chicks leave
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: another ברייתא forbids moving the basket even when the chicks are no longer on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: even though they are no longer on it, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the limit from step 19 with a ברייתא that forbids the basket even after the chicks are gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the basket stays forbidden after the chicks leave, then its usability really was taken away. The challenge to the rule returns.

phrases.english: But it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עוֹדָן עָלָיו — אָסוּר!
phrases.english: even though they are no longer on it, it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עוֹדָן עָלָיו אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limit 'only while they are on it'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids the basket even after the chicks have left.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the chicks were on it all of בין השמשות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the stricter ברייתא is about chicks that sat on the basket for all of בין השמשות. Whatever is מוקצה then stays מוקצה all שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: it is a case where they were on it for the whole of בין השמשות. Since it was set aside for בין השמשות, it was set aside for the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו settles the contradiction. The stricter ברייתא is a special case where the chicks were on the basket during all of בין השמשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item's שבת status is fixed at בין השמשות. If the basket was מוקצה then, it stays מוקצה all day even after the chicks leave. In the ordinary case, the basket is forbidden only while the chicks are on it.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who gives this answer
since (one status carries over to another)

steps.whatToRemember: If something is מוקצה during בין השמשות, it stays מוקצה for the whole of שבת (מיגו דאיתקצאי לבין השמשות איתקצאי לכולי יומא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of מוקצה: an item's status for the whole of שבת is set at בין השמשות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line.

phrases.english: where they were on it the entire twilight period.
Since it was set aside for twilight,
it was set aside for the whole day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּעוֹדָן עָלָיו כׇּל בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 and closes the basket discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the stricter ברייתא to a special case, explained by a general principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The basket stays forbidden even after the chicks leave in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It stays forbidden only if the chicks were on it all of בין השמשות; otherwise it is forbidden only while they are on it.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: no covering a fresh egg with a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rules that, just as you may not put a vessel under a hen to catch its egg, you may not turn a vessel over the egg to protect it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: just as we do not put a vessel under a hen to catch its egg, so too we do not turn a vessel over it so that it will not break.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. רבי יצחק forbids covering an egg laid on שבת with a vessel, even only to protect it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a vessel under the hen was already forbidden. רבי יצחק adds that even covering the egg, which does not make the vessel unusable, is forbidden too. Sefaria notes that this disagrees with רב חסדא, who allowed covering the egg.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת
phrases.english: Just as one may not place a vessel under a hen
to catch its egg,
so too one may not turn a vessel over it
phrases.notes: 'It' means the egg.

phrases.english: so that it will not break.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַּחַת תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling about a related topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not cover an egg laid on שבת with a vessel, even to protect it.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's reason: a vessel only for something movable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יצחק's reason: a vessel may be moved on שבת only for the sake of something that may itself be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: a vessel may only be moved for something that may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי יצחק's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not making the vessel unusable. The problem is moving a vessel to serve something מוקצה, like the egg. That is a separate, stricter reason.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this reason with אין מבטלין כלי מהיכנו. Covering the egg does not make the vessel unusable. רבי יצחק forbids it because the vessel is being moved for something מוקצה.

phrases.english: He holds: a vessel may only be moved
for something that may be moved on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: אֵין כְּלִי נִיטָּל אֶלָּא לְדָבָר הַנִּיטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel may be moved on שבת only for the sake of something that is itself movable.

steps.title: All the earlier sources are thrown at רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: All the earlier sources, which seem to allow moving a vessel for something מוקצה, are brought as challenges to רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him with all of these challenges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings all the earlier sources (vessel under a lamp, supporting a beam, vessel under a leak, and the others) as challenges to רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of those sources seems to allow moving a vessel for something that may not be moved. That goes against רבי יצחק's rule from step 23.

phrases.english: They challenged him with all these objections,
phrases.notes: Refers back to the earlier sources in the sugya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's reason from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that a vessel may be moved only for something movable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many earlier sources allow moving a vessel to serve something מוקצה.

steps.title: Answer: he needed the vessel's spot
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that all those sources are cases where the person needed the vessel's place, so moving it was allowed anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he answered: it is a case where he needs its place.
steps.whatsHappening: One answer covers every challenge. In each case the vessel was being moved for a permitted reason: someone needed the spot where it stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the vessel may be lifted for a permitted reason, you may put it down wherever you like, even next to something מוקצה. So the vessel was not really moved for the מוקצה item.

keyTerms.meaning: needs its place (the spot where it stands)

steps.whatToRemember: צריך למקומו: a vessel may be moved because you need its spot, and then it may be set down anywhere, even serving something מוקצה.

phrases.english: And he answered: where he needs its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers all the challenges of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits all the sources to one shared case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Those sources allow moving a vessel for the sake of something מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vessel was moved because its place was needed; putting it next to the מוקצה item came afterward.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows covering a fresh egg
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: a ברייתא says a fresh egg may not be used as a cover or a support, but one may cover it with a vessel so it won't break.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: an egg laid on שבת or on יום טוב may not be moved to cover a vessel with it or to prop up the legs of a bed, but one may turn a vessel over it so it will not break!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite of רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said one may not cover the egg with a vessel. This ברייתא openly allows it. That is a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a source is being brought)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Both an egg laid on Shabbat,
and an egg laid on a Festival:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָהּ לְכַסּוֹת בָּהּ אֶת הַכְּלִי
phrases.english: one may not move it to cover a vessel with it
or to prop up the legs of a bed with it,
but one may turn a vessel over it
so that it will not break!
phrases.notes: The exclamation marks the contradiction with רבי יצחק.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַחַת בֵּיצָה שֶׁנּוֹלְדָה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי יצחק after step 25's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's ruling that one may not cover the egg with a vessel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly allows covering the egg with a vessel.

steps.title: Here too, he needed the vessel's spot
steps.stepSummary: Answer: this ברייתא is also a case where the vessel's spot was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where he needs its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer as step 25 for this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessel was being moved anyway because its spot was needed. So putting it over the egg is allowed, and רבי יצחק's rule still stands.

phrases.english: Here too, where he needs its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 using step 25's principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא), reusing an earlier answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows moving a vessel just to protect the egg.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a case where the vessel was moved because its spot was needed.

steps.title: Challenge from spreading mats over stones
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: a source allows spreading mats over stones on שבת, which seems to be moving a vessel for something מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may spread mats over stones on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source against רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stones are usually מוקצה. Spreading mats over them seems to move a vessel for something that may not be moved, which goes against רבי יצחק.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצָלוֹת עַל גַּבֵּי אֲבָנִים בְּשַׁבָּת!
phrases.english: One may spread mats on top of stones on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצָלוֹת עַל גַּבֵּי אֲבָנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge to רבי יצחק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that a vessel may be moved only for something movable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mats (vessels) are spread to serve stones, which seem to be מוקצה.

steps.title: These stones are usable for the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the stones are rounded and fit for use in the bathroom, so they are not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to rounded stones that are fit for the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these particular stones are not מוקצה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rounded stones were used for wiping in the bathroom, so they have a permitted use. The mats are being spread for something movable, which fits רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, רבי יצחק's rule has two defenses. Either the vessel was moved because its spot was needed (צריך למקומו), or the item it serves is not מוקצה at all (rounded stones). More challenges follow: bricks (step 30) and the beehive (step 32).

phrases.english: With rounded stones
that are fit for the bathroom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the item is not מוקצה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stones are מוקצה, so the mats serve something מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stones have a permitted use, so they may be moved and the mats serve something permitted.

steps.title: Challenge from spreading mats over bricks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading mats over bricks on שבת. Bricks seem to be מוקצה, so this looks like using a vessel for the sake of something מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may spread mats over bricks on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source to challenge רבי יצחק. It shows a vessel, a mat, being placed over bricks to protect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bricks set aside for building are normally מוקצה because they are not for use on שבת. If you may still spread a mat over them, then a vessel is being used for the sake of something מוקצה. That goes against רבי יצחק's rule.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one may spread mats
on top of bricks on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: Bricks are normally set aside for building, so they are מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצָלוֹת עַל גַּבֵּי לְבֵנִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same chain, right after the stones challenge was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's rule that a vessel may only be used for the sake of something that may itself be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bricks are מוקצה, yet the ברייתא allows covering them with mats. So a vessel is being used for something מוקצה.

steps.title: The bricks are leftovers fit for leaning on
steps.stepSummary: The bricks are leftovers from a finished building. People lean on them, so they are not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These bricks were left over from a building, and they are fit for leaning on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these are not building bricks. They are leftover bricks that people use as seats or backrests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a building is finished, the extra bricks are no longer set aside for construction. They become everyday objects for leaning or sitting. Since they are not מוקצה, covering them with a mat is no problem for רבי יצחק.

phrases.english: These are bricks that were left over from the building,
which are fit for leaning on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bricks challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so the object is not מוקצה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bricks are building materials, which are מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bricks are leftovers used for leaning. They are usable objects, so covering them is allowed.

steps.title: Challenge from covering a beehive with a mat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows spreading a mat over a beehive on שבת to protect it from sun or rain, as long as one does not mean to trap the bees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may spread a mat over a beehive on שבת. In the sun, it is to protect it from the sun. In the rain, it is to protect it from the rain. This is allowed as long as one does not intend to trap the bees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבי יצחק. Here a mat is placed over a beehive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beehive may not be moved on שבת, so it counts as מוקצה. Yet the ברייתא allows putting a mat over it to protect it. That again looks like using a vessel for the sake of something מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: To trap (one of the forbidden מלאכות)

steps.confusionAlert: The condition 'as long as he does not intend to trap' is a separate issue, about the מלאכה of trapping. The actual challenge to רבי יצחק is only that a mat is being placed for the sake of a מוקצה beehive.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one may spread a mat
over a beehive on Shabbat,
in the sun, to protect from the sun,
and in the rain, to protect from the rain.
As long as he does not intend to trap the bees!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פּוֹרְסִין מַחְצֶלֶת עַל גַּבֵּי כַּוֶּורֶת דְּבוֹרִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge in the same chain, after the bricks challenge was answered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A beehive is מוקצה, yet one may put a mat over it to protect it. So a vessel is being used for the sake of something מוקצה.

steps.title: The beehive has honey in it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a hive that contains honey. The mat is spread to protect the honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where there is honey in the hive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hive in the ברייתא has honey inside. The mat is there to protect something of use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey is food that people want, so it is not מוקצה like the empty hive or the bees. The mat is placed for the honey's sake, not for something forbidden. So רבי יצחק's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that limits a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where there is honey in the hive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the beehive challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mat protects a מוקצה beehive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mat protects the honey, which is permitted to use. So it is allowed.

steps.title: רב עוקבא ממישן questions the honey answer
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא ממישן says to רב אשי that the honey answer works for the summer. The rest of his challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא from מישן said to רב אשי: It works out fine for the summer days...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against the honey answer. רב עוקבא first grants that it works in the summer, and his question continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תינח ('granted') accepts one part of the answer before attacking another part. The ברייתא also mentions covering the hive in the rainy season. The coming question will be about that case, which the honey answer may not cover.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine / granted (accepts one case before raising a problem with another)
רב עוקבא from the town of מישן

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא מִמִּישָׁן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Ukva from Meishan said to Rav Ashi:
Granted, this works in the summer,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא מִמִּישָׁן לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תִּינַח בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins attacking the honey answer from step 33
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the beehive contains honey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Granting the answer for the summer sets up a problem with the rainy-season case in the ברייתא. The full question continues on the next amud.
